analysis.title: GS US Daily Download 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS estimates September nonfarm payrolls rose 80k, slightly below consensus of +88k. Layoffs remain low and big data job-growth indicators picked up sequentially.

September payroll growth has tended to underperform trend when Labor Day falls later in the month, and last month's increase was boosted by leisure and hospitality and local educational services payrolls GS does not expect to repeat.

GS estimates the unemployment rate edged down to 4.0% from 4.1% in the prior month, reflecting lower continuing claims. GS forecasts average hourly earnings +0.2% month over month, below consensus, on negative calendar effects.

Adobe: Anil Chakravarthy becomes President and CEO on 12/1 as part of the leadership transition announced 3/12. David Wadhwani is stepping down to found a new venture and Adobe is appointing a permanent CFO. GS maintains a Sell rating, looking for visibility into strategic decisions and execution while competition intensifies.

GS sees the best alpha in Software over the next 12 months in companies that can move from 'AI loser' to 'AI winner', and views new Adobe leadership as a possible catalyst. Adobe's turnaround depends on modernizing its product architecture, organic investment plus targeted M&A, and converting feature adoption into monetization.

Nike F1Q results came with FY27 guidance materially below FactSet expectations and a new operating model plan called Pace. Performance business is growing (+DD%), but Sportswear (down LDD%), Jordan (down mid-teens%) and China (-26% ex-FX) are under pressure. Performance is only about 1/3 of FY26 revenue.

Nike margins are expected to come under pressure from deleverage, with the reset affecting FY27 and continuing into FY28, when Nike also laps World Cup tailwinds. GS frames the debate as whether FY27 is a trough or FY28 steps lower.

Enbridge: GS resumes coverage at Neutral. ENB is -3% YTD vs AMNA +18%. GS cites competition from added third-party pipeline capacity in Western Canada, a lower gas mix than peers in US gas pipelines, and a constrained balance sheet, despite a ~5% EBITDA CAGR through 2030.

Rates: the curve continued to bull-steepen after PCE and recent dovish Fed speak. October hike odds are down to 30% with about 3 hikes priced through year-end 2027, and the rates desk saw buyers in front-end rates.
France's fiscal consolidation plan drove cross-border moves and a flight to safety. DXY had roughly a 2 standard deviation positive move.

Equities desk: tech earnings drove ACN +16% and an investor-day move in SNPS +13%, producing big squeezes in popular shorts and perceived AI-at-risk names (GSTMTAIR +3.7%). Most hedge funds wanted to add shorts in that complex, but the desk saw more buying than selling. Activity was spotty, about 4 on a 1-10 scale, with benign client skews.
Chart of the day: Global Fundamental L/S managers finished September at -0.55%, outperforming the market benchmark.

risk_factors: Payrolls could undershoot because September growth tends to lag trend when Labor Day is late and August's leisure, hospitality and education hiring is not expected to repeat.
Nike: FY27 may not be the trough, as strategic actions continue into FY28 and the World Cup tailwind has to be lapped.
Adobe: competition intensifies and TAM growth accrues to new entrants.
Enbridge: competition in Western Canada may pressure tariff rates or rate base, and the balance sheet limits capital allocation flexibility.
Hike repricing: the market is pricing about 3 hikes through YE 2027, so a hotter payrolls print could reverse the front-end rally.
vol_and_positioning: Popular shorts and perceived AI-at-risk names squeezed higher (GSTMTAIR +3.7%) on the ACN and SNPS moves. Most hedge funds wanted to add shorts, but the desk saw more buying than selling.
Global Fundamental L/S managers finished September at -0.55%, outperforming the benchmark.
DXY had about a 2 standard deviation positive move on the flight to safety.
geopolitical: France's fiscal consolidation plan drove cross-border moves and a flight to safety.

tension_points.bull_case: Performance business is growing at a double-digit rate and strategic actions under the Pace plan aim to return the business to a healthy marketplace.
tension_points.bear_case: Sportswear, Jordan and China are under pressure, margins face deleverage, and the reset continues into FY28 when Nike laps World Cup tailwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: FY28 earnings power coming in under the scenarios GS lays out would show FY27 was not the trough.

tension_points.bull_case: New leadership is a catalyst for Adobe to leverage its core IP into AI-centric growth and move from 'AI loser' to 'AI winner'.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus sees AI headwinds, competition intensifies and TAM growth accrues to new entrants.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Visibility into bold strategic decisions followed by execution on new initiatives.
